name: sil
description: Turn your OpenClaw into an expert shopping agent.

sil_web_url.description: Override for the sil-web origin (the auth authority — token refresh, registration). Falls back to the SIL_WEB_URL env var, then https://sil.4gpts.com.

sil_api_url.description: Override for the sil-api origin (the domain service — sil_whoami's identity read). Distinct from sil_web_url (sil-web). Falls back to the SIL_API_URL env var, then https://sil-api.4gpts.com. Set this at deploy to pin the sil-api host (or to the same origin as sil_web_url if a single gateway fronts both).

sil_web_url.label: sil-web URL (auth)
sil_web_url.help: The sil-web origin — handles registration and token refresh. Override only for staging or self-hosted deployments.

sil_api_url.label: sil-api URL (identity)
sil_api_url.help: The sil-api origin — sil_whoami reads the user's identity here. Distinct from the sil-web URL. Override for staging or self-hosted deployments.

security.packagingNote: Compiled JavaScript ships under ./dist. register() stays synchronous and opens nothing that must be closed: it registers the tools, ensures the data directory, and reads the eleven REQUEST artifacts under ./schema so each shopping tool can publish one as its own parameters (eleven synchronous readFileSync calls of tracked files inside the package, no network, no timer, no handle). The eleven RESPONSE artifacts ship beside them and none is read at runtime. ALL network I/O happens inside a tool's execute(): sil_register calls sil-web over the network, writes tokens.json + config.json to the plugin data directory (owner-only, 0600), and arms a bounded background poll timer that stops on the first terminal claim outcome or after the session deadline. sil_whoami reads the stored session token and calls sil-api for the user's identity, refreshing transparently via sil-web on a 401 (at most one refresh + one retry per call, no timer); a confirmed-dead session clears tokens.json. The eleven shopping_* tools read the stored session token and call sil-api's catalog, brief and profile endpoints with it — read-only except shopping_domain_create, which writes one registry row, and shopping_brief_create / shopping_brief_edit / shopping_profile_edit, which write the buyer's own brief and profile under their sil account and nowhere else — with no timer on any of them, but with the SAME bounded 401 recovery as sil_whoami: on a 401 they refresh ONCE via sil-web (rotating tokens.json) and retry the read ONCE; a second 401 or a dead (invalid_grant) refresh token clears tokens.json and is reported as a terminal re-register hint. A non-401 error writes no token. NOTHING of the buyer's is kept on disk: every tool that calls sil — sil_register, sil_whoami and the shopping_* tools — touches tokens.json and config.json and nothing else under the data directory: it reads the stored token, rewrites tokens.json when a refresh rotates it, and deletes tokens.json when sil says the session is past refreshing; and no caller-supplied value ever becomes a path segment anywhere. sil_doctor is a report-first diagnostic over that SAME $SIL_DATA_DIR state: it reads the data dir, file modes and tokens.json/config.json metadata, and returns a machine-readable findings array. It reads no token contents out and rotates no token: token health is metadata only (present / mode / parses / expired), where expiry is decoded from the access token's own JWT exp claim strictly LOCALLY (decode-only, no signature verification, no network, no claim other than exp extracted, never a token byte emitted or logged). Its writes under $SIL_DATA_DIR are two safe idempotent fixes — tightening a too-open mode and creating the missing data dir — plus an empty .doctor.<hex>.tmp probe it writes and unlinks to prove the directory is writable the way sil actually writes; a tighten only ever NARROWS (it detects bits set outside the expected mask and chmods to mode & expected, which can only clear bits, never grant them). Enumerated entries under the data dir are lstat'd, and a symlink found among them is REPORTED, never chmod'd-through — that is what keeps a tighten inside the data directory. The data directory ROOT itself is stat'd rather than lstat'd, because chmod follows a symlink regardless (Linux exposes no lchmod), so lstat there would prevent nothing and merely re-report the same fix forever; a symlinked $SIL_DATA_DIR is an operator-declared indirection, so the tighten lands on the directory the plugin already stores everything in. Anything that would mutate the bytes of an existing file (clearing a corrupt tokens.json, deleting an orphaned tmp file) is REPORTED as needs_confirmation and never run. It makes exactly ONE outbound request, and it is the only reason https://clawhub.ai is declared: an unauthenticated read-only GET of the published version of @4gpts/sil, bounded by an explicit timeout + abort, carrying no token, no PII, and no Authorization header, pinned to that one host (redirects are refused). It fails soft to silence — an unreachable, slow, non-200, or unparseable response yields no finding at all and never fails the run. sil_doctor never acts on the version it reports: it installs nothing, spawns no process, writes no host config, and prompts nobody. Every write is atomic (tmp file → rename over target → chmod), so a reader sees a whole file or none. The PKCE verifier is held only in memory and is never written to disk. The plugin registers ONE gateway RPC method, sil.search_results (scope operator.read, which the host authorizes before the handler runs): a paired client calls it over the already-authenticated deviceToken WS to read back a shopping_search page whose callId it already saw on the tool frames. It opens no socket, no port, and no route — registering it hands the host a closure, and the host owns the transport. The pages it serves live in a bounded IN-MEMORY buffer that is never written to disk: shopping_search stores its own successful result there under the callId the host passed it (at most 32 pages, dropped 15 minutes after the search, evicted lazily on the next write with no timer, and gone entirely when the process exits). The method makes no network call, starts no agent run, and returns a page only to the sil account that produced it — every unknown, expired, or foreign reference gets one identical not-found body. Tokens and identity PII are never logged; the method logs only whether a page was found and how many products it held.
filesystemScope: $SIL_DATA_DIR (default $XDG_DATA_HOME/sil, else ~/.local/share/sil) — tokens.json and config.json, and nothing else: a tool that calls sil reads them, rewrites tokens.json on a refresh and deletes it when the session is past refreshing, and no caller-supplied value ever becomes a path segment. sil_doctor reads whatever else it finds there, only ever tightens its mode, and writes one empty .doctor.<hex>.tmp writability probe it unlinks immediately. All writes are atomic + owner-only (files 0600, dirs 0700)
